note: Two rows for one kata, split by reading. Wado-ryu teaches a single form and both rows carry the same characters 抜塞, the same five Wado organisations and the same Otsuka redaction. Both research notes name 'Passai' as the canonical form and both say to merge, so Passai is the row that survives.

Two rows for one label, split by reading. Both credit Sokon Matsumura and both route through Hohan Soken and Shito-ryu. The Passai spelling is kept because it is the form the rest of the network already points at: Itosu no Passai derives from it, and both Tachimura no Passai and Tawada no Passai are recorded against it.

Two rows for one kata, split by reading: 泊のパッサイ in Okinawan and 泊抜塞 in Japanese. Same named transmitters, Teruya Kishin then Matsumora. Tomari Passai survives as the richer record and as the target of Oyadomari no Passai, though the WKF spells it Tomari Bassai, which is kept as a variant.
